title: Database connection pool exhaustion
text: When the application reports DB_POOL_EXHAUSTED, first inspect the service and its recent logs. Confirm database availability and connection limits before changing configuration. Suggested read-only checks: systemctl status payments-api.service; journalctl -u payments-api.service -n 100 --no-pager. Escalate pool-size changes to the database owner.

title: HTTP 502 from upstream service
text: For repeated HTTP_502 responses, inspect the proxy and upstream health before taking action. Check recent service logs and the configured upstream endpoint. Suggested read-only checks: systemctl status edge-proxy.service; journalctl -u edge-proxy.service -n 100 --no-pager. Do not restart or reconfigure production services without operator approval.

title: Out-of-Memory process kill
text: The Linux kernel OOM killer terminated a process due to memory pressure. Identify the killed process from kernel logs and check current memory consumption. Read-only diagnostics: journalctl -k | grep -i 'oom' to see the kernel message, and free -h to check available memory. Do not restart the process until root cause (memory leak, undersized instance) is confirmed by an operator.

title: Disk partition full
text: A disk partition has reached 100% utilization, causing write failures. Identify the full partition with df -h and find large consumers with du -sh /* 2>/dev/null | sort -rh | head -20. Do not delete files without operator approval. Common culprits are log files in /var/log, core dumps in /var/crash, and old Docker images. Escalate if the root partition is affected.

title: TLS/SSL certificate expired
text: The service is rejecting connections because its TLS certificate has expired. Verify the certificate expiry date with: openssl s_client -connect <host>:<port> -servername <host> </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates. Certificate renewal must be performed by an authorised operator using the company PKI workflow. Do not use self-signed certificates in production.

title: CPU throttling or high load average
text: The service is being CPU-throttled (Kubernetes CFS throttling or host high load). Check container CPU limits with kubectl top pod --containers -n <namespace> and host load with uptime and top. If this is a Kubernetes pod, review CPU requests/limits in the deployment spec. Do not modify resource limits without load-testing the change first. Escalate sustained throttling above 80% to the platform team.

title: Redis connection refused
text: The application cannot connect to the Redis cache. Verify Redis is running with systemctl status redis.service or docker ps | grep redis. Check connectivity with redis-cli -h <host> -p <port> ping. Common causes: Redis process crash, network policy change, or misconfigured host/port in application config. Do not modify Redis configuration without operator approval.

title: Kafka consumer group falling behind
text: A Kafka consumer group is accumulating lag, meaning messages are produced faster than they are consumed. Check current lag with kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server <broker>:9092 --describe --group <group-name>. Increasing partition count or consumer replicas requires operator sign-off. First rule out slow consumer logic or downstream bottlenecks before scaling.
